item.title: Emergence of partially hyperbolic skew-products with circle fibers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the statistical behavior of partially hyperbolic skew-products over Axiom A diffeomorphisms using emergence. Generically, these systems satisfy the Palis conjecture: they have a finite number of physical measures whose basins together have full volume. In particular, for Lebesgue almost every point, the empirical measures converge to one of finitely many physical measures. We study the non-generic case and prove that, even when the sequence of empirical measures may have uncountably many accumulation points, these systems have low emergence.
item.dc:creator: Odylo Costa, Mauricio Poletti

item.title: Conditional limit laws for open intermittent dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.21175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain conditional limit theorems for open intermittent Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti (LSV) maps. Unlike the results of closed systems (e.g. some uniformly expanding maps), we obtain a new limit distribution, which is different from the Gaussian law or the stable law, for both "regular" and singular observables.
item.dc:creator: Can Wang, Yaofeng Su

item.title: Semisimplicity and Rigidity of the Kontsevich--Zorich Cocycle for Products of Strata
item.description: arXiv:2610.21247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Kontsevich--Zorich cocycle, its fixed tensor constructions, and their finite direct sums over products of strata of Abelian differentials. The acting groups are closed subgroups $G\subset(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$ that, up to factor permutations and coordinatewise conjugation by rotations, are products of diagonal $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$ blocks and a finite central group. For ergodic invariant probability measures, we prove Deligne-type semisimplicity: the bundles admit Hodge-compatible decompositions into $G$-invariant pieces $V_i\otimes_{A_i}W_i$, where $A_i$ are division algebras, $V_i$ carry pure variations of Hodge structure, and the multiplicity spaces $W_i$ carry finite direct sums of pure Hodge structures. Every invariant subbundle arises from $A_i$-submodules of the $W_i$. If block marginal measures have smooth local supports and are locally equivalent to smooth volume, Hodge-orthogonal projections onto invariant subbundles are locally polynomial in period coordinates on the normalized support. The proof obtains a local product-of-quadrics model and joint polynomiality from polynomiality along stable and unstable leaves. On the cone obtained by scaling each diagonal block together, projection coefficients admit homogeneous degree-zero expressions with integral powers of reciprocal block areas. For the full product group $(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$, single-stratum measure classification supplies the support hypothesis, yielding rigidity for every ergodic invariant probability measure. Under the transported support hypothesis, arbitrary coordinatewise $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$-conjugates also admit polynomial equivariant projectors, though not necessarily Hodge-orthogonal. Genus-two examples show that nonrotational conjugation can destroy Deligne-torus invariance, and independent factor scalings can require square roots of area functions.
item.dc:creator: Polina Baron

item.title: Algorithms for computing basins of attraction associated with a rational self-map of the Hopf fibration based on Lyapunov exponents
item.description: arXiv:2610.21516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The objective of this work is twofold. One, we develop a theory of iteration for complex rational functions so that the problems of overflow and indeterminacy caused by null, or almost null, denominators can be avoided when developing implementations. Second, we present easily implementable methods that allow the calculation of attracting cycles as well as the graphical representation of their basins of attraction. In order to deal with our first goal, we work with homogeneous complex coordinates, and we take the complex projective line as a model, which is expressed as a quotient of the 3-sphere through the Hopf fibration. An irreducible representation of a rational function can now be presented as a Hopf fibration endomorphism. As well as our second goal is concerned, we use Lyapunov functions and exponents to calculate the cycles associated with endomorphisms and to graphically represent the corresponding basins of attraction. We point out that our algorithms are based on the calculation of a finite set of non-negative real constants, and their calculation does not depend on the previous determination of the fixed points or attracting cycles.
item.dc:creator: V. \'Alvarez-Aparicio, J. M. Garc\'{\i}a-Calcines, L. J. Hern\'andez-Paricio, M. T. Rivas-Rodr\'{\i}guez

item.title: Density of repelling periodic points for cubic rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.21559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the repelling-density conjecture for cubic rational maps over $\mathbf C_p$: for every prime $p$, the classical Julia set is the closure of the classical repelling periodic points. By B\'ezivin's theorem, it suffices to prove that a nonempty classical Julia set contains a classical repelling periodic point. The case $p\geq5$ follows from known results for tame maps, so we treat residue characteristics two and three. We argue by contraposition, assuming that the map has no classical repelling periodic points. Maps with potential good reduction already have empty classical Julia set. Otherwise, we conjugate the map to an explicit normalized form and analyze its coefficients. In each case, we obtain coefficient restrictions and establish a uniform bound on the spherical derivatives of all iterates. This bound implies equicontinuity on the classical projective line and hence emptiness of the classical Julia set.
item.dc:creator: Nha Xuan Truong

item.title: Persistence in probability for stochastic delay equations with multiplicative noise
item.dc:creator: Mark van den Bosch, John Ioannis Stavroulakis

item.title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
item.description: arXiv:2610.21627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences. We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Melih Emin Can

item.title: Pantograph Difference Equations: Stability, Multistability, and Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2610.21635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pantograph equations are functional differential equations with proportional delay, typically involving terms of the form $x(at)$, where $0<a<1$. These equations have been studied for several decades and have applications in areas ranging from number theory to electrodynamics. In this work, we investigate pantograph difference equations as discrete dynamical maps of the form \[ x_{i+1}=F(x_{i})+G(x_{h(i)}), \qquad i\geq 0, \] where $h(i)\leq i$. In particular, we consider $h(i)=\lfloor ai \rfloor$ and $h(i)=\lfloor ai^{\alpha}\rfloor$, with $0<a<1$ and $0<\alpha<1$. We distinguish between homogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)=0$, and inhomogeneous pantograph difference equations, for which $F(x)\ne 0$. We first analyze linear pantograph difference equations and establish sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and for nonconvergence to zero. For proportional delays, analytical stability and instability regions are combined with multi-horizon parameter scans to construct regime diagrams in the $(\lambda,\delta)$-plane. We then investigate pantograph versions of the logistic and tent maps. In the homogeneous case, the dynamics evolves through step-like plateaus whose lengths increase at least exponentially, leading to slow convergence and finite-time multistability within computationally accessible time scales. In the inhomogeneous case, numerical experiments show finite-time exponential separation of nearby trajectories, consistent with chaotic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Prashant M. Gade, Sachin Bhalekar

item.title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.21945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.
item.dc:creator: Yusheng Luo, Dimitrios Ntalampekos

item.title: On effective equidistribution for product-type self-affine measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.22001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an effective equidistribution theorem on homogeneous spaces for expanding translates of product-type self-affine measures seen on unipotent orbits along any sequence of diagonal elements drifting away from walls. In particular, we do not require the diagonal elements to lie in a fixed proper and closed subcone. The main new ingredients in the proof of our equidistribution theorem include an adaptation of the methods in \cite{BHZ25} to the setting of product-type self-affine measures, as well as a weighted effective recurrence theorem for intertwined associated random walks. The latter involves decomposing the random walks according to suitable stopping times and applications of intertwined Benoist-Quint height functions.
item.dc:creator: Han Zhang

item.title: Nonpersistence of full-dimensional tori with polynomial decay in nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+T_vu+\mu|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z). \] For every $\kappa\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real Fourier multiplier $T_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $\lambda_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the Bourgain-type Diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_j\lambda_j,\mathbb Z\right) \geq\gamma_\kappa\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2\kappa})^{-1} \] for some $\gamma_\kappa>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. For this multiplier, every $3<M<4\kappa+\frac12$, every $A>0$, and all sufficiently small $\mu A^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $I_j=A\langle j\rangle^{-M}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $H^1(\mathbb T)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. This advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by Kuksin as a main open problem in KAM theory for one-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs [Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, Problem 7.1]. Bourgain discussed a related question for short-range Hamiltonian systems [Russian Math. Surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, Section 3]. The proof combines simultaneous Diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent Fourier coordinates. Uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. The mechanism suggests applications to other Hamiltonian PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Zhicheng Tong, Yong Li

item.title: Strong invariance principles in deterministic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that in every aperiodic, probability preserving dynamical system there is a function whose associated time series satisfies the almost sure invariance principle with rate asymptotically smaller then $\sqrt{n}$ and the almost sure weak invariance principle of Brosamler and Schatte.
item.dc:creator: Zemer Kosloff, Dalibor Volny

item.title: On the structure of polynomial multicorrelation sequences arising from nilpotent actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every polynomial multicorrelation sequence arising from nilpotent actions admits a decomposition into a generalized nilsequence and a null-sequence. This resolves a long-standing question of Frantzikinakis concerning the structure of polynomial multicorrelation sequences of commuting transformations. Our proof builds upon ideas underlying the norm convergence theorem of Walsh.
item.dc:creator: Jovan Andreevski, Felipe Hern\'andez

item.title: An undecidable problem in dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a variety $X$ with a self-map $\phi$ and subvarieties $Y$ and $Z$ of $X$, we consider the set of $n$ for which $\phi^n(Y)$ intersects $Z$ nontrivially. Extending a beautiful construction of Lee and Nam, we show this gives rise to an undecidable problem for a fixed ambient variety $X$ and morphism $\phi$. We further use this construction to give a counterexample to a conjecture of the author, Satriano, and Sierra.
item.dc:creator: Jason Bell

item.title: Classes of integrable metrics on Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a large new class of (weak) metrics on the Hardy space that have infinite families of conservation laws in involution. The construction of the metrics and the integrals involve the Hankel operator and a field of Nijehuis operators. The commutativity of the integrals is based on the notion of the coupling transform, which allows us to recursively construct new classes of metrics and integrals. We characterize the spectrum of the Nijenhuis operators. The paper establishes a connection between a rich class of completely integrable geodesic flows appearing in the finite dimensional Riemannian geometry and a new class of integrable systems in Banach spaces.
item.dc:creator: A. Konyaev, P. Topalov

item.title: Counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture near hyperbolic metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an LLM-assisted construction of counterexamples to the ordinary Fried conjecture, with real analytic metrics arbitrarily close to a hyperbolic metric in dimension three. For acyclic unitary line characters tending to the trivial character, the modulus of the Ruelle zeta function at zero divided by analytic torsion squared tends to zero.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Benjamin Lawton

item.title: Causal Fingerprints Reveal Hidden Mechanisms in Partially-Observed Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In partially-observed dynamical systems, distinct hidden mechanisms can produce similar observable summary statistics while explaining individual events differently. We introduce causal fingerprints: realization-dependent patterns that track how information about a hidden state is revealed through subsequent evolution. Within a prescribed dynamical model, we compare the filtering posterior, based on observations up to a given time, with the smoothing posterior, obtained after adding an expanding window of future observations. We quantify this retrospective information gain using Kullback-Leibler divergence and track its evolution as the future window of observational data expands. The fingerprint reveals both the strength and temporal reach of hidden influence, which can vary across events and their stages. Because the observed trajectory is held fixed while hidden-state inference depends on the candidate model, fingerprints reveal how competing dynamical mechanisms explain the same observations even when selected statistics agree. In linear Gaussian systems, we derive a characteristic fingerprint timescale for the temporal reach of hidden influence. Calibrated surrogates matching the observable mean, variance, and decorrelation time can still produce distinct fingerprints when feedback memory, hidden-noise memory, or hidden forcing timescales are misrepresented. Nonlinear examples reveal mechanism-dependent signatures for extreme bursts, oscillatory variability, and regime switching, including multiplicative instability versus additive forcing, deterministic nonlinear feedback versus state-dependent multiplicative noise, and intrinsic bistability versus hidden double-well forcing. Causal fingerprints therefore provide a time- and event-resolved diagnostic for asking not only whether a model reproduces observed statistics, but how its hidden dynamics explain individual events.
item.dc:creator: Zhang Jiang, Marios Andreou, Nan Chen

item.title: Seven Limit Cycles in a Periodically Forced Three-Zone Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a seven-cycle example for a periodically forced scalar equation with a continuous three-zone piecewise-linear nonlinearity. Symbolic integration and linear elimination reduce the four-flight matching conditions to two equations in the residence times. The competing exterior visits produce an additional turn of the critical response and lead to the rational parameters $(A,B,\mu)=(9,3/2,181363/100000)$. At these parameters, finite Taylor estimates give three sign changes of the return displacement. Scalar order, analyticity along transverse itineraries, and half-period reflection then establish at least seven distinct isolated periodic orbits on the phase cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Chaoyu Hu, Jizheng Chen

item.title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.21049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned dynamical models can accurately predict trajectories while producing unreliable sensitivities when differentiated or transposed, limiting their use in inverse problems and scientific decision-making. Classical adjoints provide exact local derivatives, but a single adjoint cannot represent the nonlinear response of a system to a family of finite-amplitude perturbations. We introduce SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a Koopman-based framework for inferring finite-amplitude sources. In the lifted space, the nonlinear dynamics are approximated by a linear propagator, and its transpose carries each sensor backward in a single solve. The result is a reusable lifted adjoint that predicts the measurement produced by any candidate localized event with one encoder pass and an inner product. To give the model the simulator's exact local behavior, SALTO imposes three structural constraints: it anchors the physical-state dynamics to the simulator's linearized propagator, centers the learned observables so that they vanish to second order at the reference state, and uses a block-triangular lifted propagator. These constraints guarantee that the model reduces to the simulator's tangent dynamics and classical adjoint as the amplitude vanishes, while the learned observables carry only the finite-amplitude correction. On three nonlinear PDE systems, SALTO predicts the measurements of finite-amplitude sources to within 2-8% where the classical adjoint is in error by 41-165%, recovers source position and intensity from sparse sensors nearly as accurately as inversion through the solver, and samples the joint posterior of two interacting sources, matching the solver's posterior on reaction-diffusion at a twentieth of its cost. One trained model serves new sensor layouts and measurement times with a single backward solve.
item.dc:creator: Qi Wang, Rylie Foster

item.title: Beyond 11/16: dense Kuramoto networks that resist synchrony
item.description: arXiv:2610.21271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How densely must a network of identical Kuramoto oscillators be wired before synchrony is its only stable state? The answer is a critical connectivity $\mu_c$ (the minimum degree divided by $n-1$), known to satisfy $11/16\le\mu_c<3/4$. We raise the lower bound from $11/16=0.6875$ to $\mu_c\ge(4+2q^*)/(7+q^*)=0.6929077\ldots$, where $q^*\approx0.6506$ is a root of an explicit polynomial of degree 8. The networks approaching this bound carry stable states that hug the four-cluster state: three neighboring clusters each split into two slightly separated halves, and the four crossed links between neighboring halves (those whose phase gap deviates most from a quarter turn) have densities approaching $q^*$. We build these networks from a coarse-grained cluster model, verify stability with interval arithmetic, and blow the model up into large networks with an exact minimum degree. The states are fragile and easily missed by numerical searches that impose stability margins.
item.dc:creator: Kevin P. O'Keeffe

item.title: Critical Ising Model on the Periodic Cubic Lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the critical behaviour of the nearest-neighbour Ising model on the three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^{3}$, and we present a companion set of Monte Carlo simulations. After recalling the rigorous results on the continuity of the spontaneous magnetization in $d=3$ and the triviality of the scaling limit in $d\ge 4$, we compile modern high-precision estimates of the 3D Ising critical exponents and verify the scaling relations that connect them. We then describe numerical measurements of the Binder cumulant, the magnetic susceptibility, the specific heat, the two-point correlation function, and the finite-size scaling of the magnetization. We discuss the systematic uncertainties that affect the extraction of the exponent ratios $\gamma/\nu$ and $\alpha/\nu$, and we emphasize that an exponential fit of the correlation function is not appropriate at the critical point, where the decay is algebraic.
item.dc:creator: Shenglan Yuan

item.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.21529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.
item.dc:creator: Fateme Sajadi

item.title: The role of friction on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and numerical experiments
item.description: arXiv:2610.22189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Romano, Ole Morten Aamo

item.title: Central Limit Theorem for Sequential Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2502.07765v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a general approach to establish the Central Limit Theorem with error bounds for sequential dynamical systems. The main tool we develop is the application to this setting of a projective metric on complex cones, following the ideas introduced by Rugh and Dubois. To demonstrate the power of the proposed setting, we apply it to both sequential expanding maps, where similar results are known, and to sequential dispersing billiards, for which no such results are currently known.
item.dc:creator: Mark F. Demers, Carlangelo Liverani

item.title: The unbalanced graph of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations
item.description: arXiv:2510.04989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the isomorphism of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the relation induced by the conjugacy action of the full group of an ergodic measure-preserving transformation on itself. This answers a question of Le Ma\^{i}tre in the negative and gives a positive indication towards a conjecture of Sabok. On the other hand, we prove that the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not unbalanced, which answers another question of Le Ma\^{i}tre in the negative. On the positive side, we prove that every two ergodic measure-preserving transformations are connected by a path of length two in the unbalanced graph on the set of ergodic measure-preserving transformations.
item.dc:creator: Bo Peng

item.title: Reduced-Order Inference with Structure-Preserving Parametrization for Bending and Rotating Systems
item.description: arXiv:2601.00026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mechanical systems are often characterized only by their response to certain loads known from experiments or simulations. The obtained data can be used for various purposes: system analysis, design of mathematical models, or construction of reduced-order models for further simulations under different loading conditions. The use of data for reduced-order modeling is an important developing research direction, especially when the high-dimensional system operators are unknown and their low-dimensional approximation is required for accurate but fast simulations. Our goal is to obtain the low-dimensional surrogate model from the available input signal and deformation trajectory data, capturing the correct system behavior for the basic deformation cases, namely bending and rotation, which are present in almost every complex mechanical system. In this work, we propose a methodology to infer the system operators by solving a nonlinear unconstrained optimization problem. The methodology is based on the operator inference approach for second-order systems and includes a parametrization of the unknown operators that preserves their symmetric positive definite or skew-symmetric structure. We demonstrate the performance of the novel approach for three numerical examples that are used to simulate basic bending and rotating.
item.dc:creator: Yevgeniya Filanova, Igor Pontes Duff, Pawan Goyal, Peter Benner

item.title: Affine mappings of translation surfaces: shrinking targets and Diophantine properties
item.description: arXiv:2601.02541v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a translation surface whose Veech group $\Gamma_\omega$ is a lattice. We prove that the generic orbit of the group of affine homeomorphisms of $(X,\omega)$ can be used to approximate each point of $X$ with Diophantine precision. The proof utilizes an induced $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on a fiber bundle $Y_\omega$ whose base is $SL_2(\mathbb{R})/\Gamma_\omega$ and whose fiber is a quotient of $X$. We observe that this bundle embeds as an $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit closure in the moduli space of once marked translation surfaces, and hence we may invoke the spectral gap results of Avila and Gou\"ezel and a quantitative mean ergodic theorem for the $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on the mean-zero, square-integrable functions on $Y_\omega$.
item.dc:creator: Chris Judge, Josh Southerland

item.title: On a Keller-Segel type equation to model Brain Microvascular Endothelial Cells growth's patterns
item.description: arXiv:2604.25180v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article presents a partial differential equation (PDE) of Keller-Segel (KS) type that reproduces patterns commonly observed during the growth of brain microvasculature. We provide mathematical insights into the mechanisms underlying the emergence of these patterns. In addition, we derive a data-driven equation that ensures a consistent temporal evolution of the chemoattractant associated with the observed microvascular dynamics. Beyond numerical simulations, the aim of this study is to advance a comprehensive mathematical modeling framework, spanning blood flow in cerebral arterial networks to biochemical processes, in order to better understand how vascular impairments may contribute to neurodegenerative diseases.
item.dc:creator: B Ambrosio, A Garroudji, S. Fitzsimons, H Zaag, F. M. Elahi

item.title: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: qualitative aspects
item.description: arXiv:2606.09743v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this paper is to establish polynomial Fourier decay for images of self-similar measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under sufficiently nonlinear real-analytic maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^d$. For example, we prove that if $f$ is analytic on $\mathbb{R}^k$, its graph does not lie in an affine hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^{k+d}$, and $\mu$ is not supported in an affine hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^k$, then the image measure has polynomial Fourier decay. Key steps in the proof include establishing a uniform Lojasiewicz-type inequality for self-similar measures, and using the decay of the Fourier transform of $\mu$ outside a very small exceptional set of frequencies. As an application of our results, we prove polynomial Fourier decay for self-conformal measures on $\mathbb{C}$ for a large class of complex analytic IFSs which are not self-similar but are conjugate to a linear IFS via an analytic map.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Banaji, Han Yu

item.title: Fiberwise amenability of \'{e}tale groupoids
item.description: arXiv:2608.09796v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new amenability property for \'{e}tale groupoids, termed \textit{fiberwise amenability}, along with a stronger variant termed \emph{ubiquitous fiberwise amenability}. (Ubiquitous) fiberwise amenability emerges naturally from a coarse-geometric perspective on \'{e}tale groupoids and, in the special case of transformation groupoids, it coincides precisely with the amenability of the acting group (rather than topological amenability of the action). It is also tightly linked to the existence of invariant measures on the unit space of the groupoid. The coarse-geometric framework for \'{e}tale groupoids that we develop systematically in this work allows us to establish several foundational properties of (ubiquitous) fiberwise amenability. As an application, we prove a F\o lner--paradoxical dichotomy for minimal \'{e}tale groupoids, which will serve as a key tool in a sequel on almost elementariness of \'{e}tale groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Xin Ma, Jianchao Wu

item.title: Edit distance exponents for irrational rotations
item.description: arXiv:2608.11763v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantitative edit-distance asymptotics for symbolic codings of irrational rotations $x \mapsto x+\alpha$ on $\mathbb{T}$ in terms of the irrationality exponent $\mu(\alpha)$. For the binary coding determined by an interval $[0,\beta)$, let $d_N(x,y)$ be the edit distance between the codings of the orbits of the points $x$ and $y$ up to time $N-1$. For every $\alpha \notin \mathbb{Q}$, almost every $\beta \in (0,1)$, and almost every $x,y \in \mathbb{T}$, we determine the edit-distance exponents $\displaystyle (*) \; \; \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log d_N(x,y)}{\log N} = \frac{\rho(\alpha)}{\rho(\alpha)+1} \; \;$ and $\; \; \displaystyle\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log d_N(x,y)}{\log N} = \min\Bigl\{\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{\rho(\alpha)}\Bigr\}$, where $ \rho(\alpha):=\mu(\alpha) - 1$. We find a surprising transition at the golden mean $\varphi= \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$: If $ \rho(\alpha) \le \varphi$, then both asymptotics in $(*)$ hold for all $\beta$. However, for every finite $\rho>\varphi$, there is an uncountable set of $\alpha$ with $\rho(\alpha)=\rho$ for which both edit-distance exponents are strictly smaller than the corresponding values in $(*)$ for uncountably many $\beta$. We also derive consequences for aperiodic circle homeomorphisms and Sturmian sequences. For rotations of $\mathbb{T}^d$ coded by boxes, we prove that for almost every rotation vector, the common edit-distance exponent is $d/(d+1)$.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Best, Yuval Peres

item.title: Hyperbolic area of Fatou components and new proofs of no-wandering-domain theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.23834v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a new elementary proof of Sullivan's no-wandering-domain theorem for rational maps of degree at least two using hyperbolic area. We then develop this method further to prove that a transcendental entire function has no wandering Fatou components if its set of singular values is compact and all accumulation points of that set lie in the Fatou set. Neither proof uses quasiconformal techniques.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Ye

item.title: Non-autonomous dynamics of inner functions: mixing and entropy
item.description: arXiv:2609.31476v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalise a mixing result due to Pommerenke for non-autonomous dynamical systems of forward compositions of the boundary values of centred inner functions; the proof depends on a precise bound on the orbits of such forward compositions in the unit disc. This enables us to give new criteria for such systems to have positive metric entropy, lower entropy and topological entropy. In the opposite direction, we construct a forward composition of centred degree two Blaschke products with topological entropy zero.
item.dc:creator: Vasiliki Evdoridou, N\'uria Fagella, Philip Rippon, Gwyneth Stallard

item.title: Minimum nonlinearity for pattern-forming Turing instability in a mathematical autocatalytic model
item.description: arXiv:2412.13783v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pattern formation is ubiquitous in nature and the mechanism widely-accepted to underlay them is based on the Turing instability, predicted by Alan Turing decades ago. This is a non-trivial mechanism that involves nonlinear interaction terms between the different species involved and transport mechanisms. We present here a mathematical analysis aiming to explore the mathematical constraints that a reaction-diffusion dynamical model should comply in order to exhibit a Turing instability. The main conclusion limits the existence of this instability to nonlinearity degrees larger or equal to three.
item.dc:creator: Javier L\'opez-Pedrares, Marcos Su\'arez-V\'azquez, Juan P\'erez-Mercader, Alberto P. Mu\~nuzuri

item.title: Morse theory and moduli spaces of simple polylines and polygons
item.description: arXiv:2506.06781v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that a smooth $d$-manifold $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^d$ if it admits a Lyapunov-Reeb function, i.e., a smooth map $f\colon M\to\mathbb R$ that is proper, lower-bounded, and possesses exactly one critical point. We further establish that the moduli spaces of simple polylines and positively oriented polygons with fixed or varying side lengths are diffeomorphic to Euclidean spaces, by explicitly constructing Lyapunov-Reeb functions on these spaces. This yields a refined resolution to the Carpenter's Rule Problem and settles a conjecture proposed by Gonz\'{a}lez and Sedano-Mendoza. In addition, we describe foliation structures of the moduli spaces and develop algorithms for the refolding problem.
item.dc:creator: Te Ba, Ze Zhou

item.title: The complexity of smooth words over binary alphabets
item.description: arXiv:2603.10733v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Smooth sequences over an alphabet of positive integers $\{a,b\}$ are sequences that are infinitely derivable, the emblematic example being the Oldenburger-Kolakoski sequence $\kappa$ over $\{1,2\}$. The main way to study their language is to consider a finite version of smooth sequences called smooth words. In this paper we prove that the smooth words are exactly the factors of smooth sequences and we make progress towards the conjecture that the complexity of smooth words over $\{a,b\}$ grows like $\Theta\left(n^{\log(a+b)/\log((a+b)/2)}\right)$: we prove the lower bound over any alphabet and the upper bound over even alphabets, and we improve the known upper bound over odd and mixed alphabets. We also provide a dichotomy that links the language, the morphicity and the factor complexity of $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Julien Cassaigne, Rapha\"el Henry

item.title: Bott-integrable contact forms with large systolic ratio
item.description: arXiv:2604.19237v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that there is no universal upper bound for the systolic ratio of Bott-integrable contact forms on closed 3-manifolds, thus providing further evidence for the relative flexibility of integrable contact forms. For the proof, we study piecewise linear approximations of Lutz forms and establish integrability of a `plug' constructed by Abbondandolo, Bramham, Hryniewicz and Salom\~ao for pushing up the systolic ratio.
item.dc:creator: Hansj\"org Geiges, Jakob Hedicke, Murat Sa\u{g}lam

item.title: Dynamic models with $p$ parameters are identified by $2p+1$ random features
item.description: arXiv:2607.16035v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A foundational principle in nonlinear dynamics is that the structure of a dynamical system can be recovered from a small number of generic measurements or coordinates. We develop an analogous principle for the identification of dynamic models for time series \textit{with noise}, which builds on previous identification results for noiseless dynamical systems. The noise is allowed to be non-iid, non-Gaussian, and dependent on the state. Our results cover noisily observed differential equations and discrete-time dynamical systems, as well as stochastic models with process noise. We illustrate the utility of this identification principle using a Lorenz-63 model and a H\'{e}non map model, both with observational noise.
item.dc:creator: Michael Wieck-Sosa, Cosma Rohilla Shalizi

item.title: Dynamical comparison for local homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2608.13000v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove dynamical comparison for Deaconu--Renault groupoids associated to minimal surjective non-injective local homeomorphisms of compact metrizable spaces with finite Lebesgue covering dimension. As a corollary, the associated $C^*$-algebras are UCT Kirchberg algebras, recovering results by Carlsen--Thomsen via dynamical methods. In the zero-dimensional case, our result also verifies Matui's AH-conjecture for these groupoids using a recent breakthrough of Xin Li. Our proof combines techniques from both the purely infinite and stably finite regimes: We construct partial actions of non-abelian free groups as suitable ``large subgroupoids'' and establish comparison properties for these using the paradoxical towers technique developed by Gardella--Geffen--Kranz--Naryshkin. The boundary of the subgroupoid is controlled by a groupoid version of the topological small boundary property which we deduce from finite covering dimension of the unit space. As a byproduct, we prove the classical small boundary property for minimal actions of countable discrete groups on finite-dimensional compact metrizable spaces without any freeness assumption.
item.dc:creator: Shirly Geffen, Shanshan Hua, Julian Kranz

item.title: Arbitrarily Fast Quantum Dispersion in Long-Range Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2608.27326v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct the first examples of one-dimensional long-range crystals exhibiting arbitrarily fast polynomial dispersive bounds. The Floquet functions of our Hamiltonians are highly oscillatory Weierstrass functions, whose rough autosimilar structure drives the fast dispersion. The proof develops a new Fourier decay theory for $C^\alpha$ images of the Lebesgue measure, based on a Dolgopyat-inspired transfer operator method, and yields a van der Corput lemma for Weierstrass functions. As a consequence, the local time of classical Weierstrass functions of sufficiently large lacunarity exists and is $C^k$, answering a question raised by Geman and Horowitz in 1980.
item.dc:creator: Ga\'etan Leclerc, Mostafa Sabri, Tuomas Sahlsten

item.title: Canonical expansions of $\mathbb R_{\mathcal Q}$-germs
item.description: arXiv:2609.13189v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ be the field of unary germs at $0^+$ definable in the quasianalytic o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ of Kaiser-Rolin-Speissegger. We construct a canonical ordered differential-field embedding of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ into the field of natural-support generalized Laurent series. Every unary germ has a unique such asymptotic expansion, and bounded germs have expansions with only nonnegative exponents. A germ admits a convergent generalized Laurent-series representation exactly when its canonical expansion converges; in that case, every convergent representation with well-ordered support is canonical. We also prove that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ is branching in the sense of Dembner [1]. A nonresonant hyperbolic saddle with divergent Dulac series yields a bounded positive real-analytic $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-definable germ whose canonical generalized power series diverges. This gives a negative answer to a question of Dembner asking whether every unary germ definable in a branching structure admits a convergent generalized power-series representation. Nevertheless, every bounded unary $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{Q}}$-germ has a canonical formal generalized power-series expansion. Consequently, the convergent germs form a proper ordered differential subfield of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
item.dc:creator: Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
item.description: arXiv:2610.16339v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished. The results are formalised in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Troscheit
